On Fri, Jul 10, 2027 at 7:27 PM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Irene: Can you confirm current PVC headroom + any noisy-tenant signals?

Quick technical snapshot from the initial triage (17:25–19:30 window):
- Reserved pool (pool-id: ded-az1-34) reached sustained GPU utilization >96% for ~22 minutes.
- KV cache growth on acme's model instances (context windows) increased mem pressure and triggered additional host-side queueing — this amplified tail latency.
- No obvious OOMs, but we observed a spike in context-switch waits on the serving hosts.
- One adjacent tenant had a transient QPS burst that overlapped the same window — small but timed with Acme surge (possible spillover).

Immediate mitigations I can enact (minutes):
- Trigger autoscale burst for Acme's reserved slice (requires ops/finance approval for burst credits) — moves ~30% traffic to temp instances.
- Apply per-route rate limiting for non-critical endpoints to free headroom for the fraud pipeline.
- Flip Acme to a quantized model variant (slightly lower quality) temporarily to reclaim throughput.

Risks:
- Quantized downgrade may increase false positives for fraud scoring (ops should validate thresholding).
- Burst into adjacent pool could transiently expose Acme to noisy neighbor risk unless we pin instances.

I’ll stand by on the bridge and can roll any of the three options within ~8–12 minutes once we have approval.

—Irene

Samantha —

Thanks again for the rapid report and for staying on the bridge. Summary of what we did overnight and next steps:
1) Immediate mitigation (completed 2027-07-10 20:10 PT):
   - Emergency burst authorized and applied to Acme's reserved slice (30% additional capacity routed into pinned instances in ded-az2).
   - Short-lived fallback to quantized model variant for lower latency on non-blocking endpoints.
   - Per-route rate limiting applied for lower-priority scoring calls for 40 minutes.
   - These actions brought 95th/99th latencies back down to expected SLA windows within ~9–12 minutes of activation.
2) What we found:
   - The primary driver was a sudden, sustained QPS jump from legitimate traffic combined with KV cache growth that increased serving latency. There was a coincident small burst from an adjacent tenant that likely worsened tail behavior.
3) Next steps (operational + executive):
   - Today 08:30 PT — CTO readout with Acme execs. Jonas/Vivek will join. I’ll circulate slides (timeline, root-cause, risk & mitigations).
   - We’ll run a post-incident analysis (JIRA INF-1287) to propose changes: reservation headroom policy (auto-burst thresholds), stronger per-tenant isolation on dedicated pools, and smarter eviction for KV cache under pressure.
   - Marissa will coordinate a pro-rated credit for the affected window and update your billing ledger.

Attachments: acme_error_log_20270710.txt, acme-sla-usage.csv (for your review).

Irene and the infra team will follow with a short RCA within 48 hours and remediation timeline. We appreciate your patience — we’ll ensure this is prevented in future windows.

Regards,
